propositions: The test test_rendered_output_is_byte_identical_to_the_landed_renderer kills its xdist worker on macOS py3.13 due to a per-test timeout expiry at 300s, caused by the test taking 504.8s under CPU saturation against an unbounded budget

The test walks the entire committed corpus (884 renderable units, ~1768 serial pandoc spawns) in a single monolithic loop, measuring 91.6s idle and 504.8s under saturating CPU pressure, crossing the 300s CI guard on the contended macOS lane
pytest-timeout's thread method calls os._exit(1) to kill the worker process outright, producing no traceback and causing xdist to report a crash rather than a test failure
The fix partitions the 884 units into fixed-size chunks of 40 units via pytest.mark.parametrize, making per-test cost bounded and independent of corpus size and system load

All 884 units remain compared against the oracle with real pandoc after the fix, preserving the byte-identity property the test protects, with individual chunk tests measuring ~4.37s idle (7.9x headroom under 300s guard)
A coverage guard test asserts that all chunks concatenate to exactly _renderable_units() with a total >= 100, preventing silent unit drops from parametrization
